explanations.answer: In the treasuries of the house of God
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, takes the silver, the gold and all the furnishings his father David had dedicated, and he places them in the treasuries of the house of God (2 Chronicles 5:1). The temple is done, so the gifts go inside it. Nothing gets left on the porch like a package nobody signed for.

explanations.answer: In the storerooms of his palace

The text says he placed the silver, the gold and the furnishings in the treasuries of the house of God (2 Chronicles 5:1). These were things his father David had dedicated, so they go to God's house. I'd have been tempted to keep a few cookies back, but that's me.
